name: Selena Sáenz
life: “I still remember eating at a planning desk while making a map of other people's houses.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Selena by a small Tuesday habit. Selena knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I manage the detour and have never had a route run through somebody's supper before.
appearance: Selena has close-cropped dark curls, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a brown corduroy jacket. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Selena squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Selena uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Selena well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To record what the traffic diversion costs the households.
family: Eva Bhandari is Selena’s older cousin. Selena saves a place. Eva chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Eva says, “I own the wall where the advert would hang.”
connections: Jo Johnson (local resident). A cake for the driver arrives separately from the complaint for the planner.

reactions.situation: A passenger asks to photograph a stranger through the kitchen window
reactions.response: Selena waits for the resident to give permission before a camera goes up.
